## Natural history notes

A tiny concealer moth characterized by narrow brownish to grayish wings and banded palps, though it is easily overlooked because of its small size and subtle markings. In Florida, it has been recorded in coastal and wooded habitats, including places such as Captiva and Big Cypress, and is associated with leguminous host plants in the genus Lysiloma. Adults are likely nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on host plant material and contribute to the broader food web as prey for spiders, birds, bats, and other insect-eating animals.
